research_basis.authoring_method: Original synthesis using the user brief and the THE DMI implementation reference as the structural benchmark.
research_basis.licence_handling: Original implementation content informed by Jisc structure. Jisc digital maturity materials are published under terms including CC BY-NC-SA on the main toolkit page; scenarios and practitioner language here are independently written.
notes: The source brief describes a 3-level model and requests 10 boundaries. This implementation therefore operationalises the two assessable adjacent boundaries in a 3-level model: Established to Enhanced (EM) and Enhanced to Mature (MM).
The brief also mentioned EE as a target-level code; that label is retained in metadata as an entry-threshold alias rather than a scored boundary.

objects.key_discriminator: In Organisational Digital Culture, The key shift is from emerging but uneven establishment to coordinated, cross-unit practice with clearer ownership.

common_false_positives.why_not_sufficient: Many initiatives can create the appearance of progress without any coordination or common direction.
A policy or plan does not demonstrate enhanced maturity unless it changes decisions and behaviours.

minimum_threshold_evidence: There is named ownership, a shared approach, and evidence from more than one unit.
Improvement decisions are informed by institution-level rather than purely local information.
strong_threshold_evidence: Processes, support, and expectations are consistent across most of the institution.
Coordination reduces dependence on local champions.
objects.decision_rule: Assign the lower level when evidence is inconsistent, dependent on support, or confined to unusually favourable cases.

objects.key_discriminator: In Organisational Digital Culture, The key shift is from coordination to integration, where the practice is embedded in normal planning, review, and improvement cycles.

common_false_positives.why_not_sufficient: A strong programme can still be separate from the institution's core operating model.
Recognition from peers does not guarantee mature internal integration.

minimum_threshold_evidence: The dimension is part of mainstream planning, accountability, and review.
Evidence leads to iterative improvement rather than periodic catch-up.
strong_threshold_evidence: Partnership, benchmarking, or feedback loops systematically strengthen the approach.
The institution can sustain progress through turnover, scale, or environmental change.
objects.decision_rule: Assign the lower level when evidence is inconsistent, dependent on support, or confined to unusually favourable cases.
